source_meta._title: Dimension padding doesn't affect the start piece

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21 (the exact 1.21 release, not 1.21.1 and not 24w44a or any later fixed version)
stor.environment: Single-player Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21 world with the attached dimension_padding_bug_report.zip data pack enabled before world creation. Creative mode and commands/cheats should be enabled as practical execution aids. Use a render distance sufficient to load the terrain surrounding the village; 12 chunks or greater is a practical choice, not a report requirement.
preconditions: Obtain the report attachment named dimension_padding_bug_report.zip. Use the data pack supplied with MC-272062; do not substitute a newly written pack or alter its dimension_padding value of 158.
Configure the Minecraft Launcher with an installation for the exact Java Edition 1.21 release, which is explicitly listed as affected by the report.
The executor must be able to create a new single-player world and enable commands. No seed or coordinates are supplied, so multiple plains-village searches may be necessary.
Keep the data pack enabled from the world-creation screen so that unexplored village chunks are generated using its modified plains-village structure definition.
Do not use an existing world whose nearby village chunks have already generated without the data pack.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation using the exact Java Edition 1.21 release, launch it, and wait for the main menu. Do not use 24w44a or a later version because the report lists 24w44a as the fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.21.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the single-player world creation screen by selecting Singleplayer, then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: On the Game tab, choose Creative mode and ensure commands are allowed. Creative mode is an execution aid that permits safe flight while searching; the report itself does not require a particular game mode.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands: On
steps.success_cue: The new world is configured for Creative mode and commands are enabled.

steps.action: Open the data-pack selection screen using the More tab and then Data Packs.
steps.success_cue: The Data Packs screen is visible, with areas for available and selected data packs.

steps.action: Add dimension_padding_bug_report.zip to the world-creation data-pack screen. Drag the ZIP into the Minecraft window or use Open Pack Folder and copy the ZIP into the opened folder. If Minecraft asks whether to copy the pack into the world, confirm the prompt. Keep the supplied ZIP unchanged unless the downloaded attachment was already provided as an extracted data-pack directory.
steps.success_cue: The report data pack appears in the list of available data packs.

steps.action: Enable the report data pack by selecting the arrow on its icon so it moves into the selected/enabled list, then select Done. Do not proceed while it remains only in the available list.
steps.success_cue: The report data pack is shown in the selected/enabled data-pack list and the world-creation screen is displayed again.

steps.action: Select Create New World. If a warning about experimental or unsupported data-pack settings appears, confirm that the world should be created with the selected pack. Wait through world generation without closing the game.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered the newly generated world and can move normally.

steps.action: Verify that the attachment data pack is enabled. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Inspect the enabled-pack list for a file entry corresponding to dimension_padding_bug_report.zip; its displayed pack name may differ from the attachment filename.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the report data pack among the enabled packs. If it is absent, stop and recreate the world with the pack enabled before generation.

steps.action: Remain in the Overworld and avoid manually exploring large areas before the search. This preserves ungenerated terrain for candidate plains villages.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Overworld and is ready to locate a village in terrain that has not yet been visited.

steps.action: Press T, enter the exact locate command with the leading slash, and press Enter. Record the X and Z coordinates reported for the nearest plains village. The identifier targets the plains-village structure specifically rather than another village biome variant.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports coordinates for a minecraft:village_plains structure. Record the reported X value as <VILLAGE_X> and Z value as <VILLAGE_Z>.

steps.action: Open chat and teleport directly above the reported village coordinates in Creative mode. Replace the two placeholders with the integer X and Z values from the locate result; retain Y=200. Press Enter once. This teleport into the candidate's area is the generation/loading trigger to be used for the qualifying below-Y94 village.
steps.success_cue: The player is flying at approximately Y=200 above the located village's X/Z position.

steps.action: Wait at the destination without issuing another locate or teleport command until the surrounding terrain has rendered, nearby chunks no longer appear empty, and Creative flight responds normally. Then descend vertically toward the village location without evaluating whether the village has the reported incorrect arrangement.
steps.success_cue: Terrain around the located coordinates is fully visible, movement is responsive, and the player is close enough to identify the village's central meeting-point piece.

steps.action: Identify the plains village's town-center/start piece at or near the located coordinates. Depending on the selected plains-village template, this may appear as a fountain or well, a bell with market stalls, or a bell/tree meeting-point assembly. Land on the ground-level base of that central piece, press F3 to open the debug screen, and read the Y value from the Block coordinate line. Use the ground/base level of the center piece rather than the top of a bell, roof, tree, or decorative block. Do not count or evaluate other village pieces at this stage.
steps.success_cue: The base of the candidate town-center piece has been identified and its Block Y coordinate is known. A qualifying candidate has Block Y=93 or lower; if it is Y=94 or higher, continue to step 14.

steps.action: Perform this step only when the candidate center measured Y=94 or higher. Close the debug screen with F3, fly clear of the ground, open chat, and teleport 4096 blocks east to create a substantially different search origin. After terrain and movement respond normally, return to step 10 and locate the nearest plains village again. Confirm that the next locate result differs from the rejected village; if it does not, repeat this relocation before locating again.
steps.success_cue: The player is at a distant search origin at Y=200 and is ready to repeat steps 10-13 for a different plains village.

steps.action: When the center/start-piece base is at Y=93 or lower, close the F3 debug screen if desired, stop all movement, keep the world open, and do not reload, regenerate, or use structure-placement commands. Hand control to the observation subsystem without assessing the number or arrangement of generated village pieces.
steps.success_cue: The player is beside a fully loaded plains-village town-center/start piece whose base is below Y94, and no further setup actions are pending.

stor.handoff_condition: For the final qualifying search iteration, the player has just loaded the chunks containing a naturally generated plains village whose town-center/start-piece base was verified at Y=93 or lower. The player is positioned beside that center piece in the same world with dimension_padding_bug_report.zip still enabled; begin observing the generated village structure without performing another teleport or regeneration action.
uncertainties: The raw report names the attachment but does not include its files or pack metadata. This plan assumes dimension_padding_bug_report.zip is the original functional attachment and that Minecraft 1.21 recognizes it as a data pack.
The report supplies no world seed or deterministic village coordinates. Locating a center below Y94 therefore requires a search loop, and the number of attempts cannot be predetermined.

The report says that the village must 'start below y94' but does not define an exact in-game measurement procedure. Measuring the ground/base Block Y of the town-center start piece is a practical interpretation; avoid using the height of elevated decorations.
The displayed name returned by /datapack list enabled may not exactly match dimension_padding_bug_report.zip because it can derive from the pack's metadata or directory name.
Teleporting to Y=200 and shifting the search origin by 4096 blocks are practical safety and search choices, not requirements stated by the report.

The candidate village begins generating or loading when its chunks are reached in step 11. Verifying its start-piece altitude necessarily occurs after that trigger, but the setup procedure deliberately avoids evaluating the reported visual structure outcome.
